question: The value of frac{{3({{cot }²}47^circ - se{c²}43^circ ) - 2({{tan }²}23^circ - cos e{c²}67^circ )}}{{cos e{c²}(68^circ + theta ) - tan (theta + 61^circ ) - {{tan }²}(22^circ - theta) + cot (29^circ - theta )}} is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use complementary angles: cot 47° = tan 43° and tan 23° = cot 67°.

In numerator: 3(tan² 43° − sec² 43°) − 2(cot² 67° − cosec² 67°) = 3(−1) − 2(−1) = −1.

In denominator: cosec²(68° + θ) = sec²(22° − θ) and tan(θ + 61°) = cot(29° − θ).

Denominator becomes: sec²(22° − θ) − cot(29° − θ) − tan²(22° − θ) + cot(29° − θ) = 1.

Final Value = −1 ÷ 1 = −1.

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** [3(cot² 47° − sec² 43°) − 2(tan² 23° − cosec² 67°)] ÷ [cosec²(68° + θ) − tan(θ + 61°) − tan²(22° − θ) + cot(29° − θ)]

**Formula Used:**

1. cot(90° − A) = tan A | tan(90° − A) = cot A

2. cosec(90° − A) = sec A

3. sec² A − tan² A = 1 | cosec² A − cot² A = 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fbb041816640a24bb5dee696f61b0c36e3482751f3174677f22cce447c916bcc.png] 

Step 1: Simplify the Numerator

⇒ cot 47° = tan(90° − 47°) = tan 43°

⇒ tan 23° = cot(90−23°) = cot 67°

⇒ Num = 3(tan² 43° − sec² 43°) − 2(cot² 67° − cosec² 67°)

⇒ Num = 3(−1) − 2(−1) = −3 + 2 = −1

Step 2: Simplify the Denominator

⇒ cosec(68° + θ) = sec[90° − (68° + θ)] = sec(22° − θ)

⇒ tan(θ + 61°) = cot[90° − (θ + 61°)] = cot(29° − θ)

⇒ Denom = sec²(22° − θ) − cot(29° − θ) − tan²(22° − θ) + cot(29° − θ)

⇒ Denom = sec²(22° − θ) − tan²(22° − θ) = 1

Step 3: Final Calculation

⇒ Expression = −1 ÷ 1 = −1

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Standard Pythagorean identities: sin² A + cos² A = 1, sec² A − tan² A = 1, and cosec² A − cot² A = 1.

Complementary Angle Rules

When A + B = 90°, then sin A = cos B, tan A = cot B, and sec A = cosec B.

Transformation Logic

Always check if terms can be converted to the same angle using the 90° − θ rule to apply algebraic identities.</p
